title: Works at Alexandra Gardens - External Refurbishment to 3 No. Residential Blocks of Flats
description:
Sutton Housing Partnership, on behalf of the London Borough of Sutton (LBS) is issuing a Request For Quotation (RFQ) for the Works to Alexandra Gardens - External Refurbishment to 3 No. Residential Blocks of Flats.\r
\r
Sutton Housing Partnership (SHP) Ltd. is an Arm's Length Management Organisation (ALMO), which was established in April 2006 to manage council housing owned by the London Borough of Sutton.\r
\r
While Sutton Council owns the homes and takes responsibility for housing policy and strategy, SHP is responsible for the day-to-day management of housing services to around 6,000 council tenants, which includes 1,500 leaseholder homes, 19 sheltered housing schemes, and a small number of non-domestic premises such as administrative offices, housing office hubs, and community spaces.\r
\r
This contract is being led by SHP in partnership with the London Borough of Sutton (LBS). LBS is the Freeholder of the properties, but they are managed by Sutton Housing Partnership (SHP). The dwellings are mainly occupied by LBS's tenants (i.e. social housing), whilst others are 'owned' by leaseholders (i.e. former Right to Buy properties).\r
\r
SHP provides a comprehensive tenancy management service for the tenants and assumes the role of responsible person under Regulation 3 of the Regulatory Reform Order (Fire Safety) Regulations as amended by the Fire Safety Act. This applies to the non-domestic parts of the properties, (i.e. communal areas and plant areas), however SHP also assumes the responsibilities of the 'client' under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (CDM2015).\r
\r
It is the Council's intention to appoint a Contractor, to carry out the works through this tender process (successful Tenderer). In order to robustly deliver the Works at Alexandra Gardens as outlined in the tender documents supplied. This will be determined through the tender process and the overall quality / price matrix of the submissions received.

\r

title: Tall Buildings Study - London Borough of Sutton
description:
The London Borough of Sutton is preparing a new local plan. The new plan will contain new and revised planning policies, and be supported by an objective and robust evidence base. This new local plan is set against a background of significant change in the policy context for building heights, and the role taller buildings play in shaping the size and scale of development proposals.\r
Therefore, the Council is seeking to commission a Tall Buildings Study. The study will form part of the evidence base to shape the new local plans policy approach to building heights, tall buildings, and site allocations and help guide and inform decision making on development sites and regeneration proposals across the borough.\r
\r
This study will also act as evidence to inform a character and place based approach to growth in the borough, and help inform the final stages of the emerging Characterisation Study.\r
\r
The Authority proposes to enter into a contract with the successful Tenderer for a duration of twelve months with an option to extend for a further six months. The anticipated contract commencement date is June 2023\r
\r
Please refer to the tender documents for all criteria

title: Home Care (Domiciliary Care) Flexible Framework
description:
The London Borough of Sutton (the council) intends to commission Home Care and Support services to support the independence and wellbeing of Sutton service users with care needs. It is a priority for the council that Sutton citizens are able to live independently at home. The council wishes to commission personalised, enabling and re-abling home care services which support people to retain their independence and continue to live in their own homes. The ultimate aim is that the quality of life of Sutton residents receiving home care services is enhanced.\r
\r
Home Care (Domiciliary Care) is one of the main care and support options provided to enable Service Users to maintain their independence and quality of life in their own home. The primary function of the home care service is to deliver bespoke care and support that maintains and improves wellbeing, independence and resilience appropriate to individual Service User circumstances, prevailing state of health, and personal aspirations - to live a full a life as possible: safe and independent at home.\r
\r
The London Borough of Sutton new model will be commissioned in accordance with Regulation 74 of the Public Contract Regulations 2015 (Light Touch Regime for Health and Social Care) allowing the commissioning of this contract by means of a Lot based, Flexible Framework which will be re-opened periodically as detailed within the tender documentation during the 5 year framework duration.\r
\r
The Council is seeking high quality, local Domiciliary Care Providers who are registered with, and inspected by, the Care Quality Commission (CQC) to work with us in the delivery of a new patch based service model for home care arrangements commissioned by the council on behalf of older and disabled people with assessed care needs.

OS moved to a BREEAM excellent, state of the art building in 2010. The Property is a state of the art purpose built facility on 15.75 acre site which can accommodate up to approximately 1,000 personnel. The building has a GIA of 15,669m² and total NIA of 13,898m².

Landscaped grounds surround the building which gives a picturesque outlook onto the local wildlife, with ample on-site parking for staff and visitors alike.
      
      The London office (Geovation) is a full repairing leased office based at Part Fourth Floor, Sutton Yard, London. Geovation is a department within OS which supports start-up businesses with the use of location data. This office is used by OS employees, licensees and third party start-ups.
      
      The environmental agenda continues to be a focus for the organisation, with the building strategy being a key component of the ISO14001 certification. The Facilities Management provider would play a key role in supporting OS to deliver the sustainability commitments. It is key that the provider shares the OS sustainable aspirations.

title: P2286 - Flexible Contracting Agreement for Externally Provided Day Opportunities - AWARD
description:
The Council wishes to establish a Flexible Contracting Agreement for Externally Provided Day Opportunities.  Day Opportunities, traditionally referred to as day centres, where the services are provided for people with care and support needs and their carers that take place, mainly, over daytime hours which provide vital support in two main ways:
      
      •	They provide meaningful activities, including learning, stimulation and recreation, promoting independence, supporting the development of skills, preparing for access to employment, making friends and enjoying the company of others.
      •	They provide valuable respite for unpaid carers. 
       
      Day Opportunities support autistic people, those with a learning disability, physical disabilities, acquired brain injury, older adults including those with dementia, mental health and other assessed support needs.
      
      The Flexible Contracting Arrangement (FCA) is based on the principles of a Dynamic Purchasing System. The FCA will re-open on an ad hoc basis as required; this will be at the Council's discretion and based on citizen need and market provision. There will be an initial one-off re-opening of the FCA to allow for new applications as appropriate; this includes the opportunity for unsuccessful applicants to re-apply. 
      
      The FCA will be for a period of 5 years commencing on 1 August 2025, with an option to extend for a further period of 2 years, subject to satisfactory performance and budgetary availability.  
      
      The duration of the call off contracts will be based on the individual requirements i.e. care packages; citizens' care may remain commissioned under these arrangements until such time as the call-off ends and provision will be made for this within the associated contract terms.
      
      The RTP application process for the FCA is being issued using the Council's e-tendering portal on Intend www.in-tendhost.co.uk/birminghamcc. All applications must be submitted via the appropriate portal Intend. 
      
      Use of the e-tendering portal is free throughout the whole procurement process. The system is secure and access to RTPs will only be made available to those employees of the Council and/or their authorised advisors.
      
      Deadline for receipt of initial Selection Questionnaire is noon on 11th April 2025.
